python_sdk.finding: The exact v2.1.1 migration guide states that the 2025 experimental Tasks support was removed; the 2026-07-28 revision reintroduces Tasks as official extension io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks, but this Python SDK does not implement the extension yet. Task types remain types-only. Exact release lowlevel server source has no Tasks runtime surface, and a guessed post-feature task-execution test path is absent at the release commit.

typescript_sdk_secondary_observation.finding: Current server changelog records removal of the 2025 experimental TaskManager/experimental.tasks accessors under SEP-2663. It also states that restored 2025 task wire types are interoperability-only: the task feature itself remains removed, servers do not advertise tasks, and inbound 2025 tasks/* receive -32601. Modern support docs include SEP-2663 wire/header vocabulary, but this observation is not promoted to release-pinned modern task-orchestration evidence.

cross_sdk_revision.conclusion: The requested second official SDK comparison does not yield a second durable Tasks executor in the inspected current releases. Python v2.1.1 explicitly has no official Tasks extension implementation; TypeScript current server evidence retains task wire compatibility while the old task feature remains removed. Therefore the C# v2.2.0 restart/re-entry finding must remain scoped to C# and cannot be generalized as a cross-SDK Tasks-runtime invariant.
cross_sdk_revision.safe_shared_claim: Protocol/task wire vocabulary existing in an SDK is not evidence that the SDK provides durable task orchestration, restart redrive, or full-policy-pipeline re-entry.

facts: ConversationState._save_base_state serializes the current model and writes BASE_STATE under the installed write guard.
ConversationState.__setattr__ delegates to Pydantic then immediately autosaves changed public fields when autosave is enabled and _save_depth is zero.
ConversationState.__exit__ flushes dirty state whenever depth returns to zero, regardless of whether the context exits with an exception.

Therefore an R7 implementation needs a dedicated single-snapshot commit path or equivalent temporary autosave suppression after pure validation; incremental public assignments inside or outside the existing context manager are insufficient for fail-closed recovery.
